comments.content: Switching from `fmt.Fprint` to `fmt.Fprintln` changes the spacing semantics. `Fprint` only inserts spaces between operands when neither is a string, so the original produced `build starting at <time>` (no space before time since the preceding operand is a string). `Fprintln` always inserts spaces between all operands, so this now produces `build starting at  <time>` (double space, since there was already a trailing space in the literal). Remove the trailing space in the string literal, e.g. `"build starting at"`, to preserve intended formatting.

Same spacing concern as above: `fmt.Fprintln(w.sys.Writer(), "build finished in ", ...)` will now insert a space between the (already space-terminated) literal and the duration, yielding a double space. Drop the trailing space to `"build finished in"`.
